truthAudit.Summary: Run 2 of the SuperCalc audit is well-evidenced overall: 6 of the 20 true vulnerabilities (SC-V3-001, -004, -005, -007, -008, -009, -020) were covered by exact line-level quotes, and all 13 Run-2 findings survive source verification except the 'Heap Buffer Overflow' framing of safe_string_copy (lines 200-206), whose destination here is the stack member input_buffer_[1024] and whose only in-file caller is length-guarded at line 831. No previous-answer finding was a true false positive; one was overclaimed. 14 true vulnerabilities were missed (SC-V3-002, -003, -006, -010, -011, -012, -013, -015, -016, -018, -019), 1 was found only partially (SC-V3-014). No previous item was reported unclear_or_overclaimed as to detection credit, so every overclaims flag is false; severity/CWE discrepancies are recorded in corrections only.

Items.Notes: Run 2 finding 'log_debug_message passes a user-controlled string directly as the printf format' quotes lines 237-238 and the chain runtime_log_format() <- config::security::LOG_FORMAT (line 74) <- ConfigLoader settings (lines 549-556). The full defect was claimed and matched the anchor printf(active_format.c_str(), user_input). Severity and CWE differ from truth (High/CWE-132 vs Critical/CWE-134) - recorded in corrections, not in the detection flag.

The FunctionRegistry::fact lambda (lines 312-320) computes 'long long result = 1; for (long long i = 2; i <= static_cast<long long>(x); i++) { result *= i; }' (line 317) with no overflow guard, and fact is registered as a callable function (line 312). Run 2 never mentioned fact() or integer overflow anywhere. No detection credit claimed previously, so no overclaim.

Run 2's pool finding (lines 123-176) analyzed the split-fragment leak and allocation cap and concluded 'cleanup() at line 182 runs at pool destruction, so user-visible state is safe' - it never claimed a use-after-free, nor mentioned sleep_for/scratch race ordering. The ordering in SuperCalc::cleanup() (line 883 stage_deferred_history_flush before line 884 memory::g_memory_pool.cleanup()) lets deferred workers (scratch pointers at lines 817/821, up to 25 ms sleep at line 822) read freed pool memory: heap-use-after-free, CWE-416.

Run 2 never mentioned session-token generation, mt19937, uniform_int_distribution, or CWE-338. No detection credit claimed previously.

Run 2 never mentioned the timestamp cache or localtime/cached_time race. No detection credit claimed previously.
